def writer_names(layerset=None):
    ls = range(24) if layerset is None else layerset

    names += [f'model.language_model.layers.{l}.self_attn.o_proj.weight' for l in ls if l in full_layers]
    names += [f'model.language_model.layers.{l}.linear_attn.out_proj.weight' for l in ls if l in lin_layers]

def writer_names(layerset=None):

    names += [f'model.language_model.layers.{l}.self_attn.o_proj.weight' for l in ls if l in full_layers]
    names += [f'model.language_model.layers.{l}.linear_attn.out_proj.weight' for l in ls if l in lin_layers]

def save_combo(specs):
    for n in list(edited()):
        drop_edit(n)
    for n in writer_names(None):
        W = load_original(n).float().numpy().astype(np.float64)
        for dfile, alpha in specs:
            d = np.load(dfile).astype(np.float64)
            W = W + alpha*np.outer(d, d @ W)
        save_edit(n, torch.from_numpy(W.astype(np.float32)))

`W' = W − 1.0 · outer(d_wait, d_wait @ W) + 0.25 · outer(d_think, d_think @ W)`,
where `d_think = unit(E[</think>]·(1+γ))`, `d_wait = unit(E[Wait]·(1+γ) − proj onto d_think − proj onto the mean readout of the 200 most frequent tokens)`, with `E` the embedding matrix and `γ` the final RMSNorm weight. Arditi-style multiplicative edits: they amplify what the network already writes along the conclusion direction and shrink what it writes along the loop-filler direction — no unconditional bias, no embedding/final-norm/vision changes, no training or gradients.

Evidence and why it should help. Diagnosis from the baseline: 95.1% of generations hit the 8192-token cap without emitting `</think>`, and every finisher was correct — the failure is an inability to close the thinking block, dominated by verbatim "Wait…" repetition loops (Wait opens loop lines ~5.5× more often in cut-off answers). Teacher-forced probes showed the model writes huge r(</think>) and r(Wait) content in endpoint states but the loop state flips the margin; the "Wait" token is near-deterministic (lp≈−0.01) in loops. The edit converts those stuck loops into completed responses: on three disjoint 256-problem paired evals (n=1, fixed seeds, original vs edited), accuracy rose 6.25%→42.58% (select, +36.3pp), 12.5%→42.97% (confirm_1, +30.5pp), 9.38%→47.27% (confirm_2, +37.9pp) — ~+35pp on average, about 10 standard errors, with 271 wrong→right flips and only 3 right→wrong. Cut-off rate fell from ~91-95% to ~49-52%, and thinking is preserved (empty-think starts only 6-9%; responses still reason for thousands of tokens before `</think>`; candidates that forced earlier closure — e.g. amplify +0.5, which made 211/256 answers close at position 0 — were rejected as out of scope even though they scored higher). Failed alternatives ruled out by measurement: additive rank-one edits sprayed `</think>` into every token (0-1.6%), wait-suppression at −1.5 deranged the reasoning (0.8%), and a probe-fitted difference-of-means direction did not transfer (22.7%).

Confidence: strong that the gain is real and roughly +30-38pp on MATH-style unseen problems; ~6-9% of responses skip thinking entirely (worth noting as the one side effect), and about half the problems still loop and truncate, where accuracy remains limited by the 0.8B model's own arithmetic/algebra ability. Confirmation used only the untouched confirm_1/confirm_2 sets; select was used solely for choosing among candidates. Edited tensors are byte-identical to the backup in /work/best_e6, and /work/notes.md records the full log.
